title: Restaurant website with menu
when: The user wants a site for a restaurant, bistro, pizzeria or bar with a menu and a way to book.
prompt:
Goal: A site that makes people hungry and lets them book or call in two taps.
Steps:
1. Hero with the name, cuisine in plain words and two actions: Book a table and See the menu.
2. Menu as sections (starters, mains, desserts, drinks); each dish has name, one line and price aligned for scanning.
3. Mark dietary options with short text labels (vegetarian, gluten free) and explain the labels once.
4. Booking: a form with date, time, party size, name and phone, or a clear phone link if the user prefers calls.
5. Location block with address, hours per day, a tel link and directions link.
6. Add Restaurant JSON-LD with servesCuisine, address and hours.
Quality bar:
- The menu reads well at 375 px without tiny text.
- Every form field has a visible label.
- Prices use one format.
Pitfalls:
- A menu as an image, which no one can search or read aloud.
- Booking forms that pretend to send data without a backend; say what happens.
- Dark photos with white text that loses contrast.
Verify:
- [ ] Menu uses headings and lists, not tables of images.
- [ ] Booking form has labels and a submit button.
- [ ] Hours and phone are in text.
- [ ] JSON-LD parses.
Output: index.html with menu and booking sections, style.css, and a small script only if the form needs validation.

examples.input: site for my Italian place Nonna Rita
examples.output: menu with antipasti, pasta, dolci and prices, a booking form for date, time and guests
